newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The Spraos report on measures to achieve convergence has caused friction within the government, particularly its recommendation for a one-off 10 percent charge on company profits to be used to combat unemployment. Yesterday, Prime Minister Costas Simitis ruled out any chance of the proposal being considered.
--The Bank of Greece yesterday made its first intervention in the secondary bond market, buying floaters due 2004 in intraday trade to prop up prices before the June 26 bond auction.
--National Bank of Greece is the seventh most profitable bank in Europe in relation to same capital and the only Greek bank on the list of the 100 best European banks, according to London's IBCA.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou says Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, could cooperate with the private sector to set up a new charter company free of the agreements and problems plaguing OA.

--The special charge on company profits may have been rejected for the second time in less than a week but sources say the government is seriously considering an increase in company taxation to create a special fund to combat unemployment.
--The Capital Market Commission is to consider the limits on daily trade, according to a letter to Athens Stock Exchange members.

--Public hospitals are facing massive deficits which are estimated to reach 70 billion drachmas by the end of the year. The 'black market' in health services holds close to 17 percent of the sector while the private sector is improving with 35-40 percent.

--The selection procedures for a general manager from the private sector for Greek Post Offices ELTA are in the final stretch. Five candidates are on the shortlist but reports say that the transport ministry has knocked out any candidate under the age of 45 as "too young".
--Chase Manhattan is abandoning the Greek market with two of its branches up for sale by other banks.
--Industrial production fell 0.8 percent in March this year due to to the 11.8 percent increase in the cost of manufactured goods, according to the IOBE half-yearly report.
--Insurance companies are planning on levying additional premiums for car insurance in the late summer, according to reports.

--The finance ministry has sent a circular urging cutbacks and restraint in drafting budgets for the next year. The deadline for submissions is October 31. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
